doc.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018

title: From architecture school to music education
summary: Smith enrolled in architecture but earned his A's in music, switched to music education and taught for 40 years.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you have intentions of getting an academic music career?

I didn’t have, you know watching my father and my uncles do these great musical jobs and working in the post office, and I worked in the post office, I spent five or six years from high school through college, and even my first year in New York to survive I worked in the post office. But I went to school, I enrolled in architecture school. I qualified for that and enrolled in that for my first year. And the only courses that I got A’s in were the music courses that I took. And I of course took percussion courses and got in the new percussion ensemble which was just starting in the early 1950s that hadn’t been done in colleges before. And even at that time the thought of being an architect as a back-up, I never thought about not performing music. But I figured that if I had to get a

second job in order to support a music career that I would rather not have it be the post office. So I was going to be an architect. But by my second semester it was pretty obvious that all my A’s were in the music courses and all my lower grades were in architecture, which I still love and have an appreciation for. So I switched into music education. And after that first semester my involvement and my teachers convinced me to be a music major. But by the end of five years of switching majors and going through undergraduate school I had decided that I would just get a music teaching degree so that I could remain — and I wound up doing that for 40 years. But I never thought about not being a musician.
